conflict: none — did not build, stage, or assemble
choice_reason: Both outputs fully match the brief's facts and satisfy the required interactions/states, so the decision came down to secondary dimensions. B implements real accessibility scaffolding (skip link, landmark structure, aria-live content region, role=alert/status, screen-reader table alternative for the bar chart, aria-controls/expanded/pressed wiring) while A has almost none (2 total aria-* usages in app.js, no skip link, no live region, no chart text alternative), and B's lower-friction 3-button segment toggle beats A's four cascading selects for the same job. A's single boxed 'First Reading' digest is a slightly tighter synthesis than B's distributed zone cards, but that edge doesn't offset the accessibility and interaction-cost gaps.
suspected_unblinding: none — the two builds converge closely on structure and even reuse near-identical sentences (e.g. 'Self-serve mobile web fell 27 pts — 9x the next-largest segment drop'), which is expected since both work from the same supplied facts, not a tell for either treatment.

findings.label: A
findings.description: The dynamically-built content has no ARIA live region and no screen-reader text/table alternative for the segment bar chart, so a screen-reader user gets no announcement when filters change the KPI/chart values and no non-visual read of the chart comparison.
findings.evidence: A/source/app.js contains only two aria-* attribute usages total (one decorative aria-hidden icon, one aria-pressed on a diagnostics-only button); no aria-live, no sr-only chart summary, confirmed by grep across the full 430-line file.

findings.label: A
findings.description: No skip link and no landmark elements (header/main/nav) — index.html is a bare <main id="app"></main> with everything injected by JS, so keyboard/screen-reader users have no way to jump past the repeated filter/KPI region to the analysis.
findings.evidence: A/source/index.html (13 lines total) vs. B/source/index.html which has an explicit skip-link and <header>/<main> landmarks.

findings.label: B
findings.description: The supplied evidence images for B (desktop.png, mobile.png, and all three interaction-*.png) render as completely unstyled default-browser HTML with no CSS applied at all, which would make a reviewer relying only on the images conclude the build is broken.
findings.evidence: B/desktop.png, B/mobile.png, B/evidence/interaction-01/02/03.png. Independently reproduced by serving B/source with python3 -m http.server and capturing screenshots with a locally-launched Playwright chromium (per this review's sanctioned verification method, not the shared browser tools): the same source renders fully styled, functional, and polished (colored KPI cards, working segment toggle with a real 'no data' empty state, working disclosures, working loading skeleton, correct 390px stacking). This is a packet-capture defect, not a defect in B's build, and the packet should be regenerated before being used for image-only comparisons.

findings.label: B
findings.description: The 'what remains unproven' synthesis is split across two separate cards (Largest drop / What this does and doesn't show) rather than combined into one immediately-visible digest, so assembling the full first read takes slightly more scanning than A's single boxed callout.
findings.evidence: B/source/index.html E6 and E8 articles; compare to A's single 'FIRST READING' box containing What/In whom/Unproven together (A/evidence/interaction-01-change-a-segment.png).

findings.label: A
findings.description: Four cascading select filters (device×motion segment, channel, plan intent, country) are a heavier control surface than the data supports — channel and plan-intent selections correctly show an honest 'no data for this filter combination' state, but only after the user has already clicked in and waited for it.
